newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close at new record high.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close at new record high.

text.p: Italian shares closed at a new record high on Thursday, fuelled by a new rush of orders from at home and abroad, with selected banking and telecom stocks registering hefty gains.
The all-share Mibtel index finished 3.09 percent higher at 14,825 while the blue chip Mib30 index closed 3.39 percent higher at 22,607. it was a record high for both indices.
Orders and contracts hit an all-time high of 167,757 and 105,906 respectively.
The closely-watched BCI index, tracking all listed stocks on the Milan bourse, closed on Thursday at an all-time high of 922.68.
The Italian market appeared to shake off the bout of profit-taking that has halted the bull run on most other European stock exchanges.
Star performers were Telecom Italia, which shot up 9.96 percent to 6,700 lire, Mediobanca, closing 9.29 percent at 13,100 lire and Ambroveneto, which jumped 7.12 percent to finish at 8,510 lire.
Foreign and domestic institutional buying provided the main impetus to the market but the record number of orders signalled a rush to snap up stocks by private investors.
Trading volumes rose to 3.6 trillion lire from 2.8 trillion lire on Wednesday.
The FIB30 September stock index futures contract closed 2.47 percent higher at 22,680.
Banks have performed strongly in recent sessions as investors sense the opportunity to make returns on expectations of an acceleration in the restructuring of the industry.
Insurers also played catch-up as investors piled in. Generali, which gave a presentation on Wednesday on its future business strategies, closed 5.53 percent higher at 37,765 lire.
ENI gained only 0.48 percent to close at 10,277 lire.
